summary: Pause becomes a Godot-side fact with one owner: a GamePause autoload holding a set of reasons, the single guard on the one call that advances campaign time, and a small accessibility settings surface that pauses while it is open.

coordination.notes: Godot-only lane; no Rust file is touched. godot-rust/src/strategy/tick.rs already settles the design -- there is no `paused` field in ExpeditionState, no paused branch in the tick and no host clock, so a paused game is a game whose bridge is not calling. This lane therefore adds no second answer in Rust; it makes Godot the one caller that can be stopped. game/project.godot takes an append at the END of [autoload] only, per the parallel-lane keep-both-tails rule; two other lanes append there too. campaign_session.gd is touched in exactly two hunks -- one guard call inside the existing resolve_midnight wrapper and one new function beside it -- and B8 owns that file's save/load functions. The refusal reuses the session's existing unavailable_state() dictionary with its error replaced, so no second rejection shape enters the codebase. Shipped: the guard lives inside resolve_midnight, the only call in the Godot tree that advances the strategic clock (grep over game/scripts for resolve_midnight, _process, _physics_process and Timer found no per-frame or timer-driven advance at all -- the expedition prototype's HOLD FOR MIDNIGHT button is the whole of it), so there is one guard and not a second path. The refusal reuses unavailable_state() with its error replaced, so the screen's existing 'MIDNIGHT REFUSED  -  <error>' line reports it with no change to expedition_prototype.gd. GamePause.clear() was written and then deleted before shipping because nothing called it. The three accessibility values are stored and read back and nothing else reads them, exactly as the card says.
